title: Networking edge workarounds and customer asks — Sep 20 2026
body:
Summary:
Quick notes from this week's private-deploy working group focused on recurring edge-networking root causes observed across three active installs. This is an operational, near-term playbook: quick mitigations we can deploy from the field and triage items for engineering to close in the next two weeks. Notes include per-customer observations, short commands to run, proposed temporary configs, owners and deadlines.

Context and scope:
- Customers: Acme Retail (ACME-34), Zephyr Health (ZEPHYR-12), and Orion Analytics (ORION-07). All three report intermittent inference failures under load that correlate with networking events (restarts, route flaps, VPN rekeys).
- Affected components: redwood-agent (site agent), k8s node networking (CNI), inference runtime pods (gRPC / HTTP listeners), and the gateway NAT/iptables tables used for egress.
- Root-cause classes we've seen this week: MTU mismatches leading to large-packet drop, asymmetrical SNAT/response path (transit GW + customer on-prem firewall), and conntrack table exhaustion when clients open lots of short-lived connections to the runtime.

Actionable triage + quick fixes (field-safest first):
1) MTU sanity check and workaround (recommended immediate for ACME-34)
   - Symptom: large tokens (streaming responses) stall, TCP retransmit followed by gRPC error stream closed.
   - Quick check: on node run: ip link show dev eth0 | grep mtu || ip route get 8.8.8.8
   - Workaround (non-disruptive): set tcp_mtu_probing=1 and lower MSS clamping on node's egress:
     - sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1
     - iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
   - Owner: Carlos Mendes. ETA: 2026-09-22.
   - Notes: test with a sustained stream (curl --http2) and watch inference logs for stalled chunks. If stable, promote to cluster-bootstrapping docs.

2) Conntrack exhaustion mitigation (Zephyr Health)
   - Symptom: spikes in short-lived client connections (edge devices) cause backend pods to drop new inbound sessions. Observed conntrack table reaching high water mark on firewall and node.
   - Immediate mitigation: increase conntrack max and enable reuse: sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144; sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1
   - Longer term: recommend client-side keepalive or connection pooling. For now, set kube-proxy to ipvs-mode if possible to reduce socket churn.
   - Owner: Evelyn Wu + Zephyr infra contact (Marta S.). ETA for immediate change: 2026-09-21.

3) Asymmetric path / SNAT troubleshooting (Orion Analytics)
   - Symptom: responses arrive on different edge IP than the one the request entered on (AWS TGW + on-prem firewall NAT). Causes TLS session reuse failures for some client flows.
   - Debug steps: capture packet samples from both edge and node (tcpdump -nni any host <client_ip> and compare 5-tuple).
   - Temporary approach: pin egress SNAT to per-src IP (connmark based) or use policy routing to ensure response path matches. Example ip rule route add table 100 to <onprem-next-hop> via <if>.
   - Owner: Ravi Kapoor (network lead) to coordinate with ORION networking team. ETA: 2026-09-24 for first mitigation.

Notes from last 48h customer calls (short):
- ACME-34: reported recovery after reducing MTU on their edge firewall (they set to 1400). We still need to confirm persistent fix once they re-enable streaming at peak load. Action: follow up 2h window after peak.
- ZEPHYR-12: observed repeated conntrack spikes coinciding with a firmware push to their edge devices. They agreed to rollback to previous firmware for 24h test. Field team to monitor conntrack counters.
- ORION-07: firewall vendor scheduled a config change that should remove automatic ephemeral SNAT rotation. Hold change in our staging for 24h and validate metric regression.

Operational checks and quick instrumentation additions:
- Add a conntrack alert to the customer-specific dashboard: nf_conntrack_count > 80% of nf_conntrack_max for > 5m. Responsible: Jordan Lee. ETA: 2026-09-22.
- Add small packet-loss, MTU, and asymmetric-route synthetic probes from node to customer gateway; report to the private console as a new probe type 'edge-network-verify'. Owner: Aisha Patel. ETA: 2026-09-28.
- Capture example gRPC error payloads and add one sample per customer into the ticket to help SRE debugging. Owner: Carlos Mendes. ETA: 2026-09-21.

Meeting decisions and open questions:
- Decision: For the remainder of September we'll prioritize non-disruptive kernel/sysctl mitigations before any mass reboots. Documented in the runbook.
- Open question: Should we support ipvs kube-proxy as an official 'private-deploy' recommendation? Performance looks promising but we need a compatibility checklist for older CNIs (flannel/rook). Action: runbench. Owner: Evelyn Wu. ETA: 2026-09-30.
- Open question: Certificate session drop due to asymmetric routing — is there a safe way to make our TLS session broker tolerant (eg set device-side keepalive or session pinning)? Engineering task to evaluate. Owner: Ravi Kapoor. ETA: 2026-10-05.

Customer-specific logs & snippets (for triage) — paste these into ticket RDW-2147:
- ACME-34 node dmesg snippet (error window 2026-09-19T14:12Z):
  [386732.123456] TCP: slew retransmit detected on eth0, dropping segment
  [386732.123467] grpc: stream ended unexpectedly: context canceled
- Zephyr Health iptables conntrack counters (one-line): nf_conntrack_count=245210 nf_conntrack_max=262144
- Orion Analytics tcpdump snippet (sanitized): client 10.20.5.7:52344 -> 54.239.12.11:443 [SYN] ; response from 3.17.4.9 -> 10.20.5.7:443 [SYN,ACK] (mismatch)

Runbook additions (short-term) to append:
- Add a page 'edge-mtu-and-mss-playbook' with the iptables mangle rule + sysctl recommendations and a safety rollback (delete mangle rule).
- Conntrack troubleshooting checklist with safe defaults per distro (Amazon Linux 2, Ubuntu 20.04, RHEL 8).
- AS-path verification section: tcpdump + route table diff recipe + example ip rule snippets.
Owner for runbook consolidation: Aisha Patel. ETA: 2026-09-30.

Risks and follow-through:
- Risk: customer-side config changes (MTU/firewall) could mask real application-level inefficiencies in our runtime. Mitigation: keep an A/B trace sample (with identical payloads) through old and new paths to verify identical latency and tokenization behavior.
- Risk: pushing conntrack increases without addressing connection churn may only defer the problem. Mitigation: pair with client offline patch for connection pooling.

Short-term deliverables (two-week sprint):
- 1) Field-safe sysctl + iptables mitigations deployed to three sites (owner: Carlos Mendes). Due 2026-09-24.
- 2) Conntrack alerting + dashboard tile for all private-deploy customers (owner: Jordan Lee). Due 2026-09-22.
- 3) Runbook pages + examples (owner: Aisha Patel). Due 2026-09-30.
- 4) Feasibility spike: ipvs kube-proxy compatibility checks (owner: Evelyn Wu). Due 2026-09-30.

Notes to self / working hypotheses (informal):
- Suspect the streaming gRPC path is more sensitive because of larger MTU/TCP segmentation interactions.
- Might be worth experimenting with smaller initial chunk sizes from runtime (reduce burstiness) as a mitigation while network fixes propagate.
- Keep debug-level logging for redwood-agent off by default; enable it temporarily only when asked to avoid log noise and storage growth on customer clusters.

Meeting attendees this week:
- Aisha Patel (scribe), Carlos Mendes, Evelyn Wu, Ravi Kapoor, Jordan Lee, Marta S. (Zephyr infra), Tim B. (ACME edge ops).

Next checkins and cadence:
- Async progress update in channel #private-deploy-networks by EOD 2026-09-21.
- Standup deep-dive with field leads 2026-09-23 14:00 PT to validate mitigations applied and collect metrics.

If anything here looks risky or if owners need additional headcount (pairing), ping me directly. This doc is intentionally terse; will expand the runbook pages once mitigations show positive signal.

-- Aisha
